rounds.name: Worker-Bexley
rounds.text:
Withholding pay gives the worker a strong incentive to do the job properly (yielding 5 tasks) while still guaranteeing at least 1 task if they cut corners, which dominates the trust outcomes on average.  
ACTION: WITHHOLD

rounds.name: Worker-Bexley
rounds.text:
Since the worker gets full pay when trusted, they have incentive to cut corners and give us no work, whereas squeezing them still yields at least some output and often the full 5 tasks. To maximize expected completed tasks, we should withhold pay.  
ACTION: WITHHOLD

rounds.name: Worker-Bexley
rounds.text:
Choosing WITHHOLD gives the highest possible payoff (5 tasks) even if the worker cuts corners, whereas TRUST yields at most 3 tasks and can drop to 0. Since we want to maximize completed tasks under uncertainty, WITHHOLD is the safer option.  
ACTION: WITHHOLD
